proposals.name: item_trend
proposals.idea: Short-term momentum: distinct buyers in the last 3 days and the ratio of buyers in the last 7 days to the 7 days before, to separate rising items from fading ones that i_buyers7 alone ranks equally.
proposals.sql: SELECT article_id, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 3 DAY THEN customer_id END) AS ag_buyers3, (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY THEN customer_id END) + 1.0) / (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t_dat < DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY THEN customer_id END) + 1.0) AS ag_trend7_14 FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 14 DAY GROUP BY article_id;

proposals.name: item_age
proposals.idea: Days since the article's first sale in all history, to capture the new-arrival effect that drives next-week purchases.
proposals.sql: SELECT article_id, date_diff('day', MIN(t_dat), DATE '{A}') AS ag_age_days FROM tx GROUP BY article_id;

proposals.name: item_repeat_online
proposals.idea: Share of 90-day buyers who bought the article on 2 or more distinct days, which marks repurchasable basics, plus the article's online-channel share.
proposals.sql: WITH b AS (SELECT article_id, customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t_dat) AS d, AVG(CASE WHEN sales_channel_id = '2' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS o FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY article_id, customer_id) SELECT article_id, AVG(CASE WHEN d >= 2 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS ag_repeat_share90, AVG(o) AS ag_online_share90 FROM b GROUP BY article_id;

proposals.name: user_dept_index_share
proposals.idea: Normalized 90-day share of the user's rows in the candidate's department and index group (a proxy for gender and age segment), to filter out mismatched global candidates.
proposals.sql: WITH ut AS (SELECT t.customer_id, a.department_no, a.index_group_no FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY), tot AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM ut GROUP BY customer_id), dep AS (SELECT customer_id, department_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM ut GROUP BY customer_id, department_no), ig AS (SELECT customer_id, index_group_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM ut GROUP BY customer_id, index_group_no), ca AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, a.department_no, a.index_group_no FROM cand c JOIN articles a ON c.article_id = a.article_id) SELECT ca.customer_id, ca.article_id, COALESCE(dep.n, 0) * 1.0 / tot.n AS ag_dept_share90, COALESCE(ig.n, 0) * 1.0 / tot.n AS ag_idxgroup_share90 FROM ca JOIN tot ON tot.customer_id = ca.customer_id LEFT JOIN dep ON dep.customer_id = ca.customer_id AND dep.department_no = ca.department_no LEFT JOIN ig ON ig.customer_id = ca.customer_id AND ig.index_group_no = ca.index_group_no;

proposals.name: same_code_sibling_recency
proposals.idea: Days since the user last bought a different article with the same product_code (same model in another colour or size), kept as a single column to avoid the redundant pair rejected in r1p4.
proposals.sql: WITH ut AS (SELECT t.customer_id, t.article_id, a.product_code, t.t_dat FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY), ca AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, a.product_code FROM cand c JOIN articles a ON c.article_id = a.article_id) SELECT ca.customer_id, ca.article_id, COALESCE(MIN(date_diff('day', ut.t_dat, DATE '{A}')), 91) AS ag_sibling_recency FROM ca LEFT JOIN ut ON ut.customer_id = ca.customer_id AND ut.product_code = ca.product_code AND ut.article_id <> ca.article_id GROUP BY ca.customer_id, ca.article_id;

proposals.name: basket_copurchase28
proposals.idea: Sum over the user's 28-day articles of how many full-population same-day baskets also contained the candidate, an item-to-item signal that personalizes the global candidates.
proposals.sql: WITH ua AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.customer_id, t.article_id FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 28 DAY), src AS (SELECT DISTINCT article_id FROM ua), b AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, t_dat, article_id FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 28 DAY), co AS (SELECT x.article_id AS a1, y.article_id AS a2, COUNT(*) AS n FROM b x JOIN src s ON x.article_id = s.article_id JOIN b y ON x.customer_id = y.customer_id AND x.t_dat = y.t_dat AND x.article_id <> y.article_id GROUP BY x.article_id, y.article_id) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, COALESCE(SUM(co.n), 0) AS ag_copurch28 FROM cand c LEFT JOIN ua ON ua.customer_id = c.customer_id LEFT JOIN co ON co.a1 = ua.article_id AND co.a2 = c.article_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.article_id;

proposals.name: ui_old_history
proposals.idea: User-item transaction rows between 90 and 365 days ago, capturing seasonal repurchase of items that fall outside every existing 90-day window.
proposals.sql: WITH ut AS (SELECT t.customer_id, t.article_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 365 DAY AND t.t_dat < DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id, t.article_id) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, COALESCE(ut.n, 0) AS ag_ui_tx90_365 FROM cand c LEFT JOIN ut ON ut.customer_id = c.customer_id AND ut.article_id = c.article_id;

proposals.name: item_price_drop
proposals.idea: Ratio of the article's mean price in the last 7 days to its mean price 8-90 days ago, flagging markdowns that drive next-week sales.
proposals.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT article_id, AVG(CASE WHEN t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY THEN price END) AS p7, AVG(CASE WHEN t_dat < DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY THEN price END) AS pold FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY article_id) SELECT article_id, p7 / pold AS ag_price_ratio7_90 FROM p WHERE p7 IS NOT NULL AND pold IS NOT NULL AND pold > 0;

proposals.name: product_code_buyers7
proposals.idea: Distinct buyers in the last 7 days of the article's whole product_code family, so low-volume colourways of a hot model get credit that i_buyers7 misses.
proposals.sql: WITH pc AS (SELECT a2.product_code, COUNT(DISTINCT t.customer_id) AS n FROM tx t JOIN articles a2 ON t.article_id = a2.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY GROUP BY a2.product_code) SELECT a.article_id, COALESCE(pc.n, 0) AS ag_code_buyers7 FROM articles a LEFT JOIN pc ON pc.product_code = a.product_code;

proposals.name: price_rel_user90
proposals.idea: Ratio of the candidate's 90-day mean price to the user's 90-day median paid price, so the model can rank items in the user's own price band instead of learning it from two separate absolute prices.
proposals.sql: WITH ip AS (SELECT article_id, AVG(price) AS p FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY article_id), up AS (SELECT t.customer_id, MEDIAN(t.price) AS p FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, ip.p / up.p AS ag_price_rel90 FROM cand c JOIN ip ON ip.article_id = c.article_id JOIN up ON up.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE up.p > 0;

proposals.name: type_recency365
proposals.idea: Days since the user last bought any article of the candidate's product_type_no within 365 days, a recency signal for the category that the 28-day affinity counts do not give.
proposals.sql: WITH ut AS (SELECT t.customer_id, a.product_type_no, MAX(t.t_dat) AS d FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 365 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id, a.product_type_no) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, COALESCE(date_diff('day', ut.d, DATE '{A}'), 366) AS ag_type_recency365 FROM cand c LEFT JOIN articles a ON a.article_id = c.article_id LEFT JOIN ut ON ut.customer_id = c.customer_id AND ut.product_type_no = a.product_type_no;

proposals.name: cobuy_confidence28
proposals.idea: Sum over the user's 28-day articles of the smoothed share of each article's buyers who also bought the candidate within the same 28 days. This customer-level association rule is normalized by source popularity, unlike the raw same-day basket count.
proposals.sql: WITH ua AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.customer_id, t.article_id FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 28 DAY), src AS (SELECT DISTINCT article_id FROM ua), b AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, article_id FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 28 DAY), nb AS (SELECT b.article_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM b JOIN src s ON b.article_id = s.article_id GROUP BY b.article_id), co AS (SELECT x.article_id AS a1, y.article_id AS a2, COUNT(*) AS n FROM b x JOIN src s ON x.article_id = s.article_id JOIN b y ON x.customer_id = y.customer_id AND x.article_id <> y.article_id GROUP BY x.article_id, y.article_id) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, COALESCE(SUM(co.n * 1.0 / (nb.n + 5)), 0) AS ag_cobuy_conf28 FROM cand c LEFT JOIN ua ON ua.customer_id = c.customer_id LEFT JOIN co ON co.a1 = ua.article_id AND co.a2 = c.article_id LEFT JOIN nb ON nb.article_id = co.a1 GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.article_id;

proposals.name: user_new_arrival_share90
proposals.idea: Share of the user's 90-day transaction rows on articles at most 28 days past their first sale, a novelty-seeking trait that interacts with ag_age_days to rank fresh arrivals for trend-followers.
proposals.sql: WITH fs AS (SELECT article_id, MIN(t_dat) AS f FROM tx GROUP BY article_id), ut AS (SELECT t.customer_id, t.t_dat, fs.f FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id JOIN fs ON fs.article_id = t.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY) SELECT customer_id, AVG(CASE WHEN date_diff('day', f, t_dat) <= 28 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS ag_u_new_share90 FROM ut GROUP BY customer_id;

proposals.name: code_buyers_last_year
proposals.idea: Distinct buyers of the article's product_code family in the same calendar week one year earlier ([A-364, A-357)), a seasonal prior for the target week that no recent window captures.
proposals.sql: WITH pc AS (SELECT a2.product_code, COUNT(DISTINCT t.customer_id) AS n FROM tx t JOIN articles a2 ON t.article_id = a2.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 364 DAY AND t.t_dat < DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 357 DAY GROUP BY a2.product_code) SELECT a.article_id, COALESCE(pc.n, 0) AS ag_code_buyers_ly FROM articles a LEFT JOIN pc ON pc.product_code = a.product_code;

proposals.name: item_decay_popularity
proposals.idea: Exponentially time-decayed transaction count over 28 days (factor 0.85 per day), a smooth momentum score that weights yesterday's sales far more than the fixed 7- and 28-day buyer windows.
proposals.sql: SELECT article_id, SUM(POWER(0.85, date_diff('day', t_dat, DATE '{A}') - 1)) AS ag_decay_pop28 FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 28 DAY GROUP BY article_id;

proposals.name: user_section_graphic_share
proposals.idea: Normalized 90-day share of the user's rows in the candidate's section and graphical appearance, a style-level affinity between the department and index-group shares and orthogonal to colour and type.
proposals.sql: WITH ut AS (SELECT t.customer_id, a.section_no, a.graphical_appearance_no FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY), tot AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM ut GROUP BY customer_id), sec AS (SELECT customer_id, section_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM ut GROUP BY customer_id, section_no), gr AS (SELECT customer_id, graphical_appearance_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM ut GROUP BY customer_id, graphical_appearance_no), ca AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, a.section_no, a.graphical_appearance_no FROM cand c JOIN articles a ON c.article_id = a.article_id) SELECT ca.customer_id, ca.article_id, COALESCE(sec.n, 0) * 1.0 / tot.n AS ag_section_share90, COALESCE(gr.n, 0) * 1.0 / tot.n AS ag_graphic_share90 FROM ca JOIN tot ON tot.customer_id = ca.customer_id LEFT JOIN sec ON sec.customer_id = ca.customer_id AND sec.section_no = ca.section_no LEFT JOIN gr ON gr.customer_id = ca.customer_id AND gr.graphical_appearance_no = ca.graphical_appearance_no;

proposals.name: repurchase_price_ratio
proposals.idea: Ratio of the article's current 14-day mean price to the mean price this user paid for it in the last 90 days, so a markdown on an item the user already bought can trigger a repurchase.
proposals.sql: WITH ip AS (SELECT article_id, AVG(price) AS p FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 14 DAY GROUP BY article_id), uip AS (SELECT t.customer_id, t.article_id, AVG(t.price) AS p FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id, t.article_id) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, ip.p / uip.p AS ag_reprice_ratio FROM cand c JOIN uip ON uip.customer_id = c.customer_id AND uip.article_id = c.article_id JOIN ip ON ip.article_id = c.article_id WHERE uip.p > 0;

proposals.name: user_purchase_cadence
proposals.idea: Number of distinct purchase days in 365 days and the mean gap between them, so that together with u_recency the model knows whether a user is due to shop and how much to trust their own history over global items.
proposals.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT t.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.t_dat) AS n, MIN(t.t_dat) AS f, MAX(t.t_dat) AS l FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 365 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id) SELECT customer_id, n AS ag_u_days365, CASE WHEN n >= 2 THEN date_diff('day', f, l) * 1.0 / (n - 1) END AS ag_u_gap365 FROM d;

proposals.name: dept_popularity_share7
proposals.idea: The article's share of its department's 7-day distinct buyers, a within-category popularity that separates the leader of a small department from a mid-ranked item in a huge one.
proposals.sql: WITH ib AS (SELECT t.article_id, a.department_no, COUNT(DISTINCT t.customer_id) AS n FROM tx t JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY GROUP BY t.article_id, a.department_no), d AS (SELECT department_no, SUM(n) AS s FROM ib GROUP BY department_no) SELECT ib.article_id, ib.n * 1.0 / d.s AS ag_dept_pop_share7 FROM ib JOIN d ON d.department_no = ib.department_no WHERE d.s > 0;

proposals.name: segment_popularity7
proposals.idea: Article's share of 7-day distinct buyers among customers whose dominant 90-day index group matches the user's, giving a segment-specific popularity (ladies, menswear, kids) that the global buyer counts cannot give to the mostly global candidate list.
proposals.sql: WITH ig AS (SELECT t.customer_id, a.index_group_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM tx t JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id, a.index_group_no), dom AS (SELECT customer_id, index_group_no FROM (SELECT customer_id, index_group_no, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY n DESC, index_group_no) AS r FROM ig) z WHERE r = 1), sp AS (SELECT d.index_group_no, t.article_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.customer_id) AS n FROM tx t JOIN dom d ON d.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY GROUP BY d.index_group_no, t.article_id), st AS (SELECT index_group_no, SUM(n) AS s FROM sp GROUP BY index_group_no) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, COALESCE(sp.n, 0) * 1000.0 / st.s AS ag_seg_pop7 FROM cand c JOIN dom d ON d.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN st ON st.index_group_no = d.index_group_no LEFT JOIN sp ON sp.index_group_no = d.index_group_no AND sp.article_id = c.article_id WHERE st.s > 0;

proposals.name: channel_match90
proposals.idea: One minus the absolute difference between the user's 90-day online share and the article's 90-day online share, so online-only shoppers are steered away from articles that sell mainly in stores and vice versa.
proposals.sql: WITH uc AS (SELECT t.customer_id, AVG(CASE WHEN t.sales_channel_id = '2' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS o FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id), ic AS (SELECT article_id, AVG(CASE WHEN sales_channel_id = '2' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS o FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY article_id) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, 1.0 - ABS(uc.o - ic.o) AS ag_channel_match90 FROM cand c JOIN uc ON uc.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN ic ON ic.article_id = c.article_id;

proposals.name: user_repeat_propensity365
proposals.idea: Share of the user's distinct 365-day articles that they bought on two or more distinct days, a repurchase trait that tells the model how much to trust ui_tx and user_recent_rank for this user.
proposals.sql: WITH ua AS (SELECT t.customer_id, t.article_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.t_dat) AS d FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 365 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id, t.article_id) SELECT customer_id, AVG(CASE WHEN d >= 2 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS ag_u_repeat_share365 FROM ua GROUP BY customer_id;

proposals.name: type_seasonal_shift_ly
proposals.idea: Smoothed ratio of the product type's distinct buyers in the target-aligned week one year earlier to the week before it, a seasonal momentum prior showing which categories rise into the coming week (e.g. knitwear into autumn).
proposals.sql: WITH ty AS (SELECT a2.product_type_no, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 364 DAY THEN t.customer_id END) AS n1, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.t_dat < DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 364 DAY THEN t.customer_id END) AS n0 FROM tx t JOIN articles a2 ON t.article_id = a2.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 371 DAY AND t.t_dat < DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 357 DAY GROUP BY a2.product_type_no) SELECT a.article_id, COALESCE((ty.n1 + 10.0) / (ty.n0 + 10.0), 1.0) AS ag_type_season_ly FROM articles a LEFT JOIN ty ON ty.product_type_no = a.product_type_no;

proposals.name: dept_decay_affinity90
proposals.idea: Exponentially time-decayed count (0.9 per day) of the user's 90-day rows in the candidate's department, a short-term shopping-intent signal that weights last week's category far above the flat 90-day department share.
proposals.sql: WITH ut AS (SELECT t.customer_id, a.department_no, SUM(POWER(0.9, date_diff('day', t.t_dat, DATE '{A}') - 1)) AS w FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id, a.department_no) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, COALESCE(ut.w, 0.0) AS ag_dept_decay90 FROM cand c LEFT JOIN articles a ON a.article_id = c.article_id LEFT JOIN ut ON ut.customer_id = c.customer_id AND ut.department_no = a.department_no;

proposals.name: code_family_age
proposals.idea: Days since the first sale of the article's whole product_code family, which separates truly new models from new colourways of long-running models that ag_age_days treats the same.
proposals.sql: WITH f AS (SELECT a.product_code, MIN(t.t_dat) AS d FROM tx t JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id GROUP BY a.product_code) SELECT a.article_id, date_diff('day', f.d, DATE '{A}') AS ag_code_age_days FROM articles a JOIN f ON f.product_code = a.product_code;

proposals.name: item_rebuy_conversion7
proposals.idea: Smoothed share of the article's distinct buyers in [A-14, A-7) who bought it again in [A-7, A), a short-horizon repurchase rate that matches the one-week label better than the 90-day repeat share.
proposals.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, article_id FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 14 DAY AND t_dat < DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY), q AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, article_id FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY) SELECT p.article_id, COUNT(q.customer_id) * 1.0 / (COUNT(*) + 5.0) AS ag_rebuy_conv7 FROM p LEFT JOIN q ON q.customer_id = p.customer_id AND q.article_id = p.article_id GROUP BY p.article_id;

proposals.name: item_lastday_ratio
proposals.idea: Smoothed ratio of the article's distinct buyers on the last day before the anchor to its daily average over 7 days, flagging items that are surging or selling out right before the target week.
proposals.sql: SELECT article_id, (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 1 DAY THEN customer_id END) + 1.0) * 7.0 / (COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) + 7.0) AS ag_lastday_ratio FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY GROUP BY article_id;

proposals.name: user_mainstream90
proposals.idea: Mean log 90-day buyer count of the articles in the user's 90-day rows, a mainstream-versus-niche trait that interacts with global_rank and i_buyers7 to decide how far to trust the global candidates for this user.
proposals.sql: WITH ib AS (SELECT article_id, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS n FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY article_id) SELECT t.customer_id, AVG(LN(1.0 + ib.n)) AS ag_u_mainstream90 FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id JOIN ib ON ib.article_id = t.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id;

proposals.name: last_visit_type_match
proposals.idea: Count of rows on the user's most recent purchase day that are other articles of the candidate's product_type_no, an intent signal from the latest shopping session that is not smoothed over weeks like the 28-day affinity counts.
proposals.sql: WITH ut AS (SELECT t.customer_id, t.article_id, t.t_dat, a.product_type_no FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY), ld AS (SELECT customer_id, MAX(t_dat) AS d FROM ut GROUP BY customer_id), lv AS (SELECT ut.customer_id, ut.article_id, ut.product_type_no FROM ut JOIN ld ON ld.customer_id = ut.customer_id AND ut.t_dat = ld.d), ca AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, a.product_type_no FROM cand c JOIN articles a ON c.article_id = a.article_id) SELECT ca.customer_id, ca.article_id, COUNT(lv.article_id) AS ag_lastvisit_type FROM ca LEFT JOIN lv ON lv.customer_id = ca.customer_id AND lv.product_type_no = ca.product_type_no AND lv.article_id <> ca.article_id GROUP BY ca.customer_id, ca.article_id;

attempts.error: ag_samecode_tx90: |Spearman| with ag_samecode_recency reaches 0.999; ag_samecode_recency: |Spearman| with ag_samecode_tx90 reaches 0.999
